english.title: Master of/seaman in ship in UK port or waters omit to do act required for safety of ship, equipment or persons on board
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the master of]_
(B)_[a seaman employed in]_

**(..SPECIFY SHIP..),

(C)_[a United Kingdom ship,]_
(D)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was in a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY UK PORT..),]_
(E)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was within United Kingdom waters while proceeding to a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY UK PORT..),]_
(F)_[a ship which was registered under the law of **(..SPECIFY COUNTRY OUTSIDE THE UNITED KINGDOM..) and was within United Kingdom waters while proceeding from a United Kingdom port, namely **(..SPECIFY UK PORT..),]_

while on board the ship or in its immediate vicinity, omitted to do an act required to

(G)_[preserve the ship or its machinery, navigational equipment or safety equipment from being lost, destroyed or seriously damaged]_
(H)_[preserve a person on board the ship from death or serious injury]_
(I)_[prevent the ship from causing the loss or destruction of or serious damage to another ship or structure, or the death of or serious injury to a person not on board the ship]_

in that **(..SPECIFY ACT OMITTED..),

(J)_[that omission being deliberate or amounting to a breach or neglect of duty]_
(K)_[you being under the influence of drink or a drug at the time of the omission]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 58(2)(b) and (5) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being the master/seaman
of ship registered under law of a country outside UK
in UK port / waters while proceeding to / from UK port
while on board the ship or in its immediate vicinity
omitted to do act required to preserve the ship / machinery / navigational / safety equipment
from being lost / destroyed / damaged
OR preserve a person on board ship from death / serious injury
OR prevent ship from causing loss / destruction / serious damage to another ship / structure
OR death / serious injury to a person not on board the ship
that omission being deliberate / amounting to a breach or neglect of duty
OR the defendant being under the influence of drink or a drug at the time of the omission

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove where the act alleged against the accused constituted a breach or neglect of duty that the accused took all reasonable steps to discharge that duty - section 58(6)(a)
(ii) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove that at the time of the act alleged against the accused he was under the influence of a drug taken by him for medical purposes and either that he took it on medical advice and complied with any directions given as part of that advice or that he had no reason to believe that the drug might have the influence it had - section 58(6)(b)
(iii) In proceedings for an offence it shall be a defence to prove;
(a) that he could have avoided committing the offence only by disobeying a lawful command, or
(b) that in all the circumstances the loss, damage, destruction, death or injury in question, or (as the case may be) the likelihood of its being caused, either could not reasonably have been foreseen by the accused or could not reasonably have been avoided by him - section 58(6)(d)
(iv) See section 58(8) for the definitions for 'breach or neglect of duty', 'duty' and 'structure'

Note that a master, officer or seaman referred to options (D), (E) or (F) of the above wording cannot commit an offence as outlined in option (G) of the wording - section 58(7)

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
